affectedPublicSurfaces: New infra/systemd unit files (juli-celery-worker.service, juli-celery-beat.service) — inert until a human manually copies them to /etc/systemd/system/ on the VPS and runs `systemctl daemon-reload` + `enable --now`. This PR does not modify infra/scripts/deploy-release.sh, .github/workflows/release.yml, or any currently-enabled unit (juli-api.service, juli-web.service, juli-secrets-refresh, juli-restore-drill), so merging and even deploying this PR's code changes causes zero behavior change to the live public site until a human takes that separate manual step.

docs/runbooks/app-review-runbook.md and infra/scripts/env/api.env.example — documentation/example-config updates only (install steps, package list, Redis/Celery env-var guidance); no behavior change on their own.

candidateVerificationJourney.restrictedRoute: This slice ships two new, unreferenced systemd unit files plus docs/example-config updates — nothing in the deploy pipeline is modified to install, enable, or start them automatically. A merge to main and even a full deploy-release.sh run on the VPS does not start these units, because deploy-release.sh only restarts juli-api/juli-web (unchanged in this PR) and never touches systemd unit installation for other units. Verification is therefore: (1) confirm the two new unit files are syntactically valid and follow juli-api.service's exact ExecStartPre/EnvironmentFile/WorkingDirectory/Restart pattern; (2) confirm the Celery commands match the real module path (juli_backend.workers.celery_app) and that no schedule is invented beyond what celery_app.py's beat_schedule already declares; (3) confirm the runbook/env-example diff is additive documentation only, touching no script or existing unit's content; (4) a human, separately and after this merges, installs redis-server, uncomments the Redis/Celery env vars in the real /etc/juli/api.env (via AWS Secrets Manager per the existing secret flow), copies the two new units, and enables them — that activation step is explicitly out of scope for this PR and is not automated by it.

journeys.entryUrl: infra/systemd/juli-celery-worker.service, infra/systemd/juli-celery-beat.service (static file review, no live host)
assertions: systemd-analyze verify (or equivalent static parse) succeeds on both new unit files

both units follow juli-api.service's exact pattern: ExecStartPre=/root/Juli-AI-v2/infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh, EnvironmentFile=/etc/juli/api.env, WorkingDirectory=/root/releases/current, User=root, Restart=on-failure, RestartSec=5

ExecStart uses the real venv path (/root/releases/current/.venv/bin/celery) and the real app module (juli_backend.workers.celery_app), matching juli-api.service's ExecStart convention of pointing at /root/releases/current/.venv/bin/
juli-celery-beat.service does not redefine or hardcode a schedule — it only runs `celery ... beat`, relying entirely on celery_app.py's existing beat_schedule dict

neither unit is referenced by, added to, or made a dependency of deploy-release.sh, release.yml, or any existing unit's WantedBy/After chain — confirming both are inert until a human manually installs them

migrationCompatibility.notes: No Alembic migration in this PR and no database schema change. Once a human later enables these units on the VPS, they invoke existing Celery tasks (e.g. mock_analytics_hourly_reconcile) against the existing schema via existing repositories — no new schema dependency introduced here. New unit files reference only environment variables already documented in infra/scripts/env/api.env.example (REDIS_URL, CELERY_BROKER_URL, CELERY_RESULT_BACKEND) — no new, previously-undocumented secret key introduced by this PR.

rollbackAssertion.preCutoverFailureBehavior: There is no cutover in this PR — the new unit files are not referenced anywhere in the automated deploy path, so a defect found in review is simply fixed before merge; there is no live-traffic risk either way since nothing auto-activates.
rollbackAssertion.postCutoverFailureBehavior: Not applicable to this PR's automated deploy — merging and deploying it does not start any new process. If, after a human LATER manually installs redis-server and enables these units on the VPS (a separate, explicitly out-of-scope-here action), the worker/beat process misbehaves, the rollback is `sudo systemctl disable --now juli-celery-worker juli-celery-beat` — a simple, always-available stop, since these are brand-new units with no prior state or in-flight work to reconcile. juli-api and juli-web are entirely unaffected either way.

doNotInfer: Do not add the new units to infra/scripts/deploy-release.sh's automated flow in this PR — installation stays a documented manual step per the runbook, matching how the existing 5 units were bootstrapped.

Do not invent a Celery Beat schedule value beyond what celery_app.py's beat_schedule dict already declares — if code declares no schedule for some future task, do not add one to the systemd unit or runbook; that is a separate, later decision.
